title: Total gamechanger, even if you own other Zojirushi rice cookers
text:
Total gamechanger, even if you own other Zojirushi rice cookers. Even though I could have purchased the same model locally in Japan for much less, I made the choice to purchase a Zojirushi made for the US market (120 v). This was important to me for a number of reasons: not only for the convenience of having English menus and documentation, but also the fact that rice cookers in Japan run on 100v, and unless used with a step-down transformer, can burn out much more quickly on US voltage. Since I make rice almost daily, I wanted a rice cooker that would work in both Japan as well as the US and one that offered a number of functions.

So when I had the chance to test out Zojirushi’s updated Umami model (NL-GAC10) I jumped at the chance. Not only does it have settings like jasmine, quick jasmine, sushi, mixed rice and brown rice, but it also has a setting just for quinoa and Zojirushi’s exclusive umami mode, which soaks the rice longer to produce a moist, fluffy rice. The Umami model also comes with a steamer basket, making it easy to quickly steam veggies, fish, or eggs and create a complete meal.

I love the fact that it has settings not found on other rice cookers, particularly the GABA brown rice setting. GABA brown rice is sprouted brown rice that is much higher in gamma-aminobutyric acid and fiber and is said to be more easily digestible. It requires a long soaking and heating process (using the GABA Brown Rice setting activates the GABA in the brown rice by soaking it for two hours at 104°F before cooking), but the resulting rice is fluffy, moist, and flavorful. And those looking for traditional breakfast options like congee or okayu will find special modes for those as well. Another unique feature is the “slow cook” setting, which lets you make soups and stews right in the rice cooker, and the rewarming feature to bring cooked rice to the perfect serving temperature.

The timer function makes it easy to have perfect rice ready and waiting in the morning to make bento boxes, or have dinner ready when you get home (takikomi gohan is a favorite in my household).

I put the Umami Micom through its paces making several batches of umami, sushi rice, GABA brown rice, mixed rice, and basmati rice cooked on the jasmine setting, as well as following Zojirushi’s recipe for slow cooker minestrone and caprese rice salad. You’ll also find a wealth of other great recipes on their website at https://www.zojirushi.com/app/recipe/rice-cookers and Just One Cookbook’s website.

The Zojirushi Umami micom rice cooker is incredibly versatile; whether you’re shopping for your first Japanese rice cooker or an appliance that can handle a variety of tasks from steaming to slow cooking to making perfect white, brown, jasmine, and sushi rice, the Zojirushi Umami Micom (available in 5.5 and 10-cup size) is the perfect all-in-one appliance, especially if your family eats rice or grains daily.
